_comment: The Frame Gate. Written once at C4 anchor per ADR-001 (TypeScript + Node + Vitest). Declared, never inferred.
_test_notes: tsc --noEmit sits INSIDE test_command by ADR-001 action 6. Six of nineteen refusals (REF-01, REF-02, REF-06, REF-09, REF-12, REF-17) demand rejection at parse rather than at runtime, so a transpile-only run would bypass a third of the guard set. test_command is the gate: full suite, unscoped. test_module is the inner loop and is never a gate. test_select runs one named test and is what the mutation battery invokes with the Test name column from S3 section 5.
reviewer_command: claude -p --agent k7-reviewer --model claude-fable-5-1 --output-format text --allowedTools "Bash(npx tsc:*)" "Bash(npx vitest:*)" "Bash(python3 tools/rederive.py:*)" "PowerShell(npx tsc:*)" "PowerShell(npx vitest:*)" "PowerShell(python3 tools/rederive.py:*)" "Write(.k7/**)" "Edit(.k7/**)"
_scaffold_notes: Carries the built-in defaults (.metaframework/, tools/, the emission contract, IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE, HARNESS) because an array REPLACES rather than extends. SETUP.md is dropped from the list: it is deleted, not exempted. The two Phase rosters are ADDED because they are digest-pinned in roster-manifest.json — editing them to substitute a placeholder would fail the rosters check, and their placeholder is content (they document the filename template CLAUDE_<Concept>_Phase3.md) rather than leakage, which is the same reason the emission contract is exempt by default. governance/S3/ stays NON-exempt: an unsubstituted placeholder in a frozen spec is a real defect.
_reviewer_notes: R-01, accepted 2026-09-10. The previous invocation used --permission-mode acceptEdits, which auto-approves EDITS - the one thing K7 must never do - and leaves Bash requiring an approval that, under -p, no human is present to give. So every command was denied, across two rounds, while the charter orders execution in CC-4, CC-5 and CC-6. acceptEdits is dropped (a reviewer that can edit can quietly become a builder) and replaced with an allowlist of exactly the declared commands. This does not widen the tool grant - Bash is already in the agent's charter - it stops silently denying what the charter assigned. VERIFY the --allowedTools syntax against the installed CLI with tools/k7-run.py --dry-run before relying on it: an unrecognised flag would fail open into the same silent denial it replaces.
_rederive_notes: rederive_all drives the harness' own vector runner, which is tools/rederive.py - the only rederive tool in the tree. It previously named tools/rederive-impl.ts, which has never existed: a placeholder written at C4 that no check caught because MOD-02 pins no vector, so nothing invoked it. K7 round 1 (CC-5) found it by reading rather than running. It would have failed at MOD-04, the first vector-bearing module. rederive_invoke is separate and correct: it is how rederive.py drives THIS implementation, and its {entry}/{input_file} placeholders are filled per vector. R-36 (2026-10-13): rederive_invoke runs the vector harness tools/vectors/run.ts with the vector id, the implementing file ({entry}, so impl_sha pins the implementation) and the input file. The harness lives in tools/ because a src/ file cannot read an input file without naming an external (REF-02).
_isolation_notes: R-03 migration. new-object.py writes each class's OS-12 test as tests/<stem>.isolation.test.ts, so the filter '.isolation.test' selects exactly those (tests/ports/external-isolation.test.ts does not match: its stem is '-isolation.test'). The seal runs this with the environment cleared. Until MOD-03 lands there are no isolation tests and vitest exits non-zero on an empty selection; that is the seal's concern, not a gate defect now.
